pk.context: 200 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

pill.desc: white capsule with a coloured band, band colour varies by strength

tell: A high fat meal delays this COX-2 inhibitor's peak by 1 to 2 hours while raising total absorption 10% to 20%.

clues.text: Absolute bioavailability has not been studied, and food increases total absorption by 10% to 20%. Protein binding is about 97%, and the drug is mainly cleared by CYP2C9 metabolism.
Molecular weight 381.4, and it is practically insoluble in aqueous media at physiological pH.
Approved under an NDA in strengths from 50 mg to 400 mg; doses up to 200 mg are given twice daily.

Boxed warning on serious cardiovascular and gastrointestinal events. Contraindicated around bypass graft surgery and with sulfonamide allergy; dyspepsia and abdominal pain are common reasons for stopping.
Relief of osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis from age 2, ankylosing spondylitis, acute pain in adults and primary dysmenorrhea.
It is believed to work by inhibiting prostaglandin synthesis, primarily through inhibition of the enzyme COX-2.
The generic name begins with C and has nine letters.
